sentences.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di doted on the bright boy and kept him always near.

sentences.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」

translations.literal: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'
translations.idiomatic: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'

sentences.zh: 惠帝乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Hui broke off his greeting.

sentences.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。

translations.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.
translations.idiomatic: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.

sentences.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。

translations.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.
translations.idiomatic: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."

sentences.zh: 由是奇之。

translations.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」

translations.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'
translations.idiomatic: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」

translations.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'
translations.idiomatic: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."

sentences.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。

translations.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.

sentences.zh: 文明元年八月，奉高宗神主祔於太廟中，始遷宣皇帝神主于夾室。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Wenming, Gaozong's spirit tablet was enshrined within the Grand Temple; for the first time, Emperor Xuan's spirit tablet was moved to the side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Wenming 1, eighth month: Gaozong's tablet was enshrined in the Grand Temple, and Xuan's tablet was moved to the side chamber for the first time.

sentences.zh: 垂拱四年正月，又於東都立高祖、太宗、高宗三廟，四時享祀，如京廟之儀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Chuigong, three temples for Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong were also established in the eastern capital; the four seasonal offerings followed the rites of the capital temples.
translations.idiomatic: Chuigong 4, first month: the eastern capital gained temples to Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong, with seasonal rites matching the capital.

sentences.zh: 別立崇先廟以享武氏祖考。

translations.literal: A separate Chongxian Temple was established to offer to the Wu clan ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: A separate Chongxian Temple was built for Wu clan ancestors.

sentences.zh: 則天尋又令所司議立崇先廟室數，司禮博士、崇文館學士周忭希旨，請立崇先廟為七室，其皇室太廟，減為五室。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian soon again ordered the offices to deliberate on how many chambers the Chongxian Temple should have; Court of Spring Rites erudite and Scholar of the Chongwen Institute Zhou Ping, to please her intent, requested seven chambers for Chongxian Temple and reduction of the imperial ancestral temple to five chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian soon ordered debate on Chongxian's chamber count; Zhou Ping of Spring Rites, courting her wish, urged seven chambers for Chongxian and five for the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 春官侍郎賈大隱奏曰：「臣竊准秦、漢皇太后臨朝稱制，並據禮經正文，天子七廟，諸侯五廟。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Court of Spring Rites Jia Dayin memorialized, saying: "Your subject ventures to cite Qin and Han, when empress dowagers held court and exercised regulatory power—all followed the canonical ritual texts: the Son of Heaven has seven temples, feudal lords five temples.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dayin of Spring Rites wrote: "Qin and Han dowagers who ruled from court all cited canon—the Son of Heaven keeps seven temples, lords five.

sentences.zh: 蓋百王不易之義，萬代常行之法，未有越禮違古而擅裁儀注者也。

translations.literal: This is the unchanging meaning of the hundred kings, the constant law of myriad generations—never has anyone transgressed ritual and antiquity to arrogate regulation of ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: That is the immovable rule of kings and ages—none has broken ritual to rewrite ceremony at will.

sentences.zh: 今周悰別引浮議，廣述異文，直崇臨朝權儀，不依國家常度，升崇先之廟而七，降國家之廟而五。

translations.literal: Now Zhou Cong cites floating opinions and broadly sets forth heterodox texts, directly elevating provisional rites of holding court, not relying on the state's constant norms—raising Chongxian temple to seven while lowering the state temple to five.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Cong now cites loose opinion and stray texts, exalting a regent's provisional rite over state norm—seven for Chongxian, five for the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣聞皇圖廣辟，實崇宗社之尊；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard: when the imperial design is broadly opened, it truly honors the altars of state;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard: when the throne's design is wide, the altars of state gain honor;

sentences.zh: 帝業弘基，實等山河之固。

translations.literal: when the imperial enterprise has a vast foundation, it truly equals the solidity of mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: when its foundation is vast, it matches mountains and rivers in firmness.

sentences.zh: 伏以天步多艱，時逢遏密，代天理物，自古有之。

translations.literal: Your subject observes: the heavenly steps have been many times arduous; times encountered mourning seclusion; one who substitutes for Heaven and governs things has existed since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's course has been hard; times of mourning seclusion came; regents who govern for Heaven are ancient.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇太后親承顧托，憂勤黎庶，納孝慈之請，垂矜撫之懷，實所謂光顯大猷，恢崇聖載。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully considers: the Empress Dowager personally received the entrustment, labored in care for the common people, accepted the request of filial piety and compassion, extended a cherishing and soothing heart—this truly is what is called to glorify the great plan and expand the sage burden.
translations.idiomatic: The Dowager took the trust, toiled for the people, heard pleas of filial mercy, and soothed the realm—truly glorifying the great design and widening the sage charge.

sentences.zh: 其崇先廟室，合同諸侯之數，國家宗廟，不合輒有移變。

translations.literal: Chambers of Chongxian Temple should accord with the feudal lord count; the state ancestral temple must not casually be shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxian should match a lord's count; the state temple must not be casually altered.

sentences.zh: 臣之愚直，並依正禮，周忭之請，實乖古儀。」

translations.literal: Your subject's stubborn directness wholly follows orthodox ritual; Zhou Ping's request truly contravenes ancient ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's stubborn directness wholly follows orthodox ritual; Zhou Ping's request truly contravenes ancient ceremony."

sentences.zh: 則天由是且止，

translations.literal: Zetian therefore stopped for the time being,
translations.idiomatic: Zetian held off for the moment.

sentences.zh: 及吳平，太康初詔復爵。

translations.literal: When Wu pacified Taikang early edict restored noble.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang restored his rank after Wu fell.

sentences.zh: 有司奏封江陽王，帝曰：「睦退靜思愆，改修其德，今有爵土，不但以赦。

translations.literal: Relevant offices memorialized enfeoff Jiangyang prince emperor said 'Mu retiring quiet pondering faults reform cultivating virtue now possessing noble territory not only because amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Relevant offices memorialized enfeoff Jiangyang prince emperor said 'Mu retiring quiet pondering faults reform cultivating virtue now possessing noble territory not only because amnesty.

sentences.zh: 江陽險遠，其以高陽郡封之。」

translations.literal: Jiangyang peril remote therefore use Gaoyang commandery enfeoff him.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyang peril remote therefore use Gaoyang commandery enfeoff him.'

sentences.zh: 乃封為高陽王。

translations.literal: Thereupon enfeoffed Prince of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He became prince of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 元康元年，為宗正。

translations.literal: Yuankang year one became Grand Director of Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang named him imperial clan director.

sentences.zh: 薨於位，世子蔚早卒，孫毅立。

translations.literal: Died in office heir apparent Wei died early grandson Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in post; grandson Yi followed after heir died young.

sentences.zh: 拜散騎侍郎，永嘉中沒于石勒，

translations.literal: Appointed irregular cavalry gentleman middle Yongjia lost to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Yi fell to Shi Le during Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 隆安元年，詔以譙敬王恬次子恢之子文深繼毅後。

translations.literal: In the first year of Long'an, Edict appointed Prince Jing Tian second son Huizhi son Wenshen continuing Yi posterity.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Long'an, the court assigned Wenshen from Huizhi's line to continue Yi.

sentences.zh: 立五年，薨，無嗣，復以高密王純之子法蓮繼之。

translations.literal: Established five years died without heirs again using Gaomi prince Chun son Falian continuing him.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later Falian continued the extinct line from Gaomi house.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song accepted abdication state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song abolished the principality.

sentences.zh: 輔弟翼

translations.literal: Fu di Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi—Fu's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 翼字子世，少曆顯位，官至武賁中郎將。

translations.literal: Yi courtesy Zishi in youth successively held eminent posts and reached Major of the Household Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi, styled Zishi, rose young to major among the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 武帝未受禪而卒，以兄邕之支子承為嗣，封南宮縣王。

translations.literal: Before Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he died; Yong's cadet son Cheng was appointed successor as Prince of Nangong county.
translations.idiomatic: He died before the Wei-Jin transition; Yong's collateral heir Cheng took Nangong county.

sentences.zh: 薨，子祐嗣立，承遂無後。

translations.literal: He died; son You succeeded and Cheng thereby had no posterity.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng died You continued the line, ending Cheng's branch.

sentences.zh: 翼弟下邳獻王晃

translations.literal: Yi di Xiapi Offering Wang Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, Prince Xian of Xiapi—Yi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 弈至黃門郎，先望卒。

translations.literal: Yi reached Yellow Gate Gentleman and died before Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi rose to yellow-gate gentleman but died before his father.

sentences.zh: 整亦早亡。

translations.literal: Zheng also died young.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng likewise died young.

sentences.zh: 以弈子奇襲爵。

translations.literal: By Yi's son Qi the noble rank was inherited.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed to Yi's son Qi.

sentences.zh: 奇亦好畜聚，不知紀極，遣三部使到交廣商貨，為有司所奏，太康九年，詔貶為三縱亭侯。

translations.literal: Qi also delighted in hoarding wealth without limit, sending three divisions of agents to trade in Jiao and Guang; after officials memorialized against him, an edict in Taikang year nine demoted him to Marquis of Sanzong Precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Qi also delighted in hoarding wealth without limit, sending three divisions of agents to trade in Jiao and Guang; after officials memorialized against him, an edict in Taikang year nine demoted him to Marquis of Sanzong Precinct.

sentences.zh: 更以章武王威為望嗣。

translations.literal: Next Prince Wei of Zhangwu was made Wang's successor.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then named Sima Wei of Zhangwu as Wang's heir.

sentences.zh: 後威誅，復立奇為棘陽王以嗣望。

translations.literal: Later when Wei was executed, Qi was again established as Prince of Jiyang to succeed Wang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei's execution Qi was restored as Prince of Jiyang to continue Wang's line.

sentences.zh: 隨穆王整，兄弈卒，以整為世子。

translations.literal: Prince Mu of Sui, Zheng—when elder brother Yi died Zheng was made heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died Zheng became heir of the Yiyang house.

sentences.zh: 曆南中郎將，封清泉侯，先父望薨，追贈冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He successively held General of the Southern Gentlemen, was enfeoffed Marquis of Qingquan; he died before his father Wang; when Wang died he was posthumously invested Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded southern gentlemen and held Qingquan marquis but predeceased Sima Wang; upon Wang's death the court posthumously named him Champion General.

sentences.zh: 武帝以義陽國一縣追封為隨縣王。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu used one county of the Yiyang state to posthumously enfeoff him as Prince of Sui county.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu carved out Sui county from Yiyang for his posthumous princedom.

sentences.zh: 子邁嗣。

translations.literal: Son Mai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Mai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 太康九年，以義陽之平林益邁為隨郡王。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taikang Pinglin of Yiyang was added to enlarge Mai as Prince of Sui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 288 Yiyang's Pinglin canton enlarged Mai's domain to prince of Sui commandery.
